There are ongoing discussions through the Catalyst team to resolve this issue. While these discussions are pending, we are resubmitting our proof-of-achievement for milestone 1 including only long-form educational articles.

ms.report:
Dear Reviewers, thank you for the positive reviews.
Here are our answers to the two questions asked by the third reviewer:
> We may benefit more by knowing the reviews that were given to these proposals, both accepted or rejected, than just a comprehensive table, if you offer a reason why doing otherwise is sitll fine, that will be accepted as well
As usual for any academic workshop or conference, the peer reviews must be kept confidential. The reviews are sent to the paper authors directly by the Easychair system keeping also the identity of the reviewers secret. So the authors know that the papers were reviewed by members of the program committee, but they don't know the subset of program committee members who reviewed their papers. This approach is known as "blind review" and it is deemed to improve the quality of the peer review process, since it allows the program committee members to be critical of the papers without fearing retaliation.
Note that this approach is different from Catalyst's approach, where the identity of the reviewers is still kept secret, but the reviews themselves are public. There are probably advantages and disadvantages in both approaches. But we are following the usual academic approach, and thus revealing the reviews here (even while keeping the identities of the reviewers secret) would violate the implicit expectations of both authors and program committee members when they decided to participate in the workshop's peer review process.

> There is an accepted submission with no affiliation, Pseudonym or identifier. Can you offer an explanation for this?
Some authors prefer to submit their papers without author or affiliation, so that the reviewers are not influenced by their identity in the evaluation of their papers. This is known as "double blind review". Some workshops and conferences make "double blind review" obligatory.
